anuppuccin.label: AnuPpuccin · Dracula
anuppuccin.accentBehavior: Choosing a preset sets its default accent; workspace accentColor remains customizable. Runtime active-control ink selects Crust when it meets 4.5:1, then white when it meets 4.5:1, with a black/white fallback for middle luminance. The initial Flamingo uses Crust ink.
anuppuccin.headingDividers: H1/H2 use a 1px currentColor rule and .2em bottom inset in full Markdown, Files Markdown and BlockNote headings. Compact Tags/library readers retain their local geometry.
anuppuccin.folderBehavior: Each parent restarts the twelve-tone order among its sibling folders, including descendants. WeakMap caching follows tree identity. Explicit folder colors and resolved Iconize colors precede automatic colors.

narrative.overview:
This records the incumbent visual system, rather than a new identity. The authority is `src/index.css`, the existing Sidebar, TagsView, NoteCard, and the running desktop interface. New local surfaces inherit this shell; their own layout decisions stay in surface briefs.

The implemented Tags finder supplies a scoped extension, evidenced by `src/components/TagsView.css` and the approved actual viewport. Its dense rows, mint tag markers and quiet reading area use the incumbent shell and semantic tokens. The `tags-` entries below describe this surface; they do not replace the global type or shape vocabulary.

The implemented All Notes library supplies a second scoped extension, evidenced by `src/components/NotesGallery.css` and the finished desktop, narrow and reading captures. Its `library-` entries retain the incumbent palette and font family while recording the library's content cards, context contrast and compact controls. Surface composition and acceptance evidence stay in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-components-notesgallery-tsx.md`.

The implemented Files and Trash workspace supplies a scoped extension, evidenced by `src/components/fileBrowser.css`, the shared `FileBrowser` and the finished dark desktop, narrow and Trash captures. Its `files-` entries record a dense work table, a current-folder route, selection actions and a collapsible properties region. It inherits the same Inter family, dark surfaces and violet interaction states. Surface direction and delegated-choice provenance stay in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-components-filesview-tsx.md`; operation details stay in `docs/FILES_BROWSER.md`.

The implemented workspace shell supplies an approved shell extension, evidenced by `src/components/workspace.css`, `WorkspaceChrome`, `Sidebar`, and the finished desktop and narrow captures. It keeps the incumbent palette while adding docked utility chrome, document tabs and a bounded active work region. The `workspace-` entries describe the shell itself; the specific Obsidian reference, pinned composition and quality bar stay in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-app-tsx.md`. Existing local views retain their own scoped systems inside the work region.

The implemented Calendar workspace supplies a scoped extension, evidenced by src/components/calendar.css, CalendarView, CalendarTaskRow, CalendarWeek and the finished synthetic review captures. Its calendar- entries retain the incumbent Inter family, dark semantic surfaces and violet interaction states while recording local source colors, compact date context and bounded planning controls. Direction, composition, benchmark limits and review acceptance stay in .impeccable/surfaces/src-components-calendarview-tsx.md. Local light overrides were tested with synthetic semantic tokens; the application still ships the established dark palette.

The optional AnuPpuccin · Dracula preset supplies a user-selected color system, evidenced by `src/themes/anuppuccin.css`, the current settings application and the reviewed desktop/narrow captures. The incumbent color tokens and violet descriptions below continue to describe the Synapse preset, which remains the default for new and older workspaces. AnuPpuccin rebinds those semantic roles only when selected: it preserves the established fonts, type ramp, shapes, layout and local surface behavior. The `anu-` tokens record the imported palette and supported reading/folder colors; the direction and verification scope stay in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-themes-anuppuccin-css.md`.

The implemented Canvas supplies a scoped extension, evidenced by `DrawioCanvas.tsx`, `whiteboardBlock.tsx`, `drawio.css` and the synthetic desktop/narrow captures. The complete local draw.io 32.4.1 browser editor owns drawing interaction inside the existing fullscreen flow. The host inherits the workspace semantic palette and Inter UI family; the local iframe retains its separate dark editor chrome. The `drawio-` entries record host title, control and context roles while reusing the established control radius. Direction, recovery behavior and the browser/native verification boundary stay in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-editor2026-blocks-whiteboard-drawiocanvas-tsx.md`; integration details stay in `docs/drawio-canvas.md`.

rules.name: The Semantic Accent Rule
rules.body: Within Tags, mint identifies tag membership and tag filters; violet identifies the selected note, active pane, match mode, links and focus. Keep those meanings distinct.

rules.name: The Library Accent Rule
rules.body: Within All Notes, mint identifies tags; violet identifies focus, selection, the previewed card and the primary New note action.

rules.name: The Files Accent Rule
rules.body: Within Files and Trash, violet marks selection, keyboard focus, destinations and primary actions; mint identifies note tags, lavender identifies uncustomized folders, and the local danger role identifies destructive actions. Preserve user-assigned folder colors.

rules.name: The Workspace Active Label Rule
rules.body: Document tabs use a strong foreground label with a link-colored icon and underline. Other active shell labels retain the link role, and context uses the secondary foreground. Keep selection and keyboard focus distinct.

rules.name: The Calendar Source Rule
rules.body: Within Calendar, violet marks the selected date, today, completion, focus and primary actions; amber identifies local task previews, blue identifies external events and lavender identifies notes and journal marks. Preserve user task colors as task metadata, and pair source color with text or outline icons.

rules.name: The Dense Context Rule
rules.body: Small type carries metadata and compact tag summaries; note titles, search and primary actions remain visually stronger. Preserve the observed small interface steps instead of enlarging every row or flattening the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Calendar Detail Rule
rules.body: Within Calendar, the smallest type carries cell times, counts and narrow hour context. Task titles, editable fields and the selected-day plan remain stronger; a full accessible date label and reachable day plan provide the detailed reading path.

rules.name: The Active Work Region Rule
rules.body: Tabs retain destinations and the shell renders only the active content. Preserve the work area's available width and reachable panel controls when either side pane collapses or overlays it.

rules.name: The Files Row Rule
rules.body: Keep Files and Trash rows at their fixed height while windowing the list. Long names truncate with their full title available; narrow layouts remove secondary columns instead of turning rows into variable-height cards.

rules.name: The Calendar Hour Bounds Rule
rules.body: Within the hourly week, keep the combined task/event previews at two inside the fixed hour row and retain a reachable overflow action. The day plan exposes the complete paged lists instead of increasing slot height.

rules.name: The Explicit Quick Look Rule
rules.body: A selected note does not read its body until quick look is explicitly requested. Show loading, retry and truncation states in the properties region, and keep image references as inert attachment labels.

rules.name: The Calendar Date Context Rule
rules.body: Within Calendar, period arrows follow the displayed anchor while preserving a useful selected day. Changing month/week/list retains the chosen date; opening a compact day plan transfers focus after commit, and closing it restores a visible date target or pane toggle.

rules.name: The Explicit Preset Rule
rules.body: Synapse remains the default. Apply the AnuPpuccin palette only after an explicit workspace choice; switching back restores the Synapse palette and its default accent. Selecting either preset sets its default accent, after which the accent remains customizable.

rules.name: The Folder Override Rule
rules.body: In AnuPpuccin, derive automatic folder tones from each folder's order among sibling folders, including descendants, and repeat the twelve-tone sequence independently within each parent. Cache that mapping per tree identity; explicit folder colors and resolved Iconize colors retain precedence over automatic tones.

rules.name: The Reading Color Rule
rules.body: Apply the six heading colors and supported code, quote and table roles as rendering styles. Preserve Markdown bytes, editor instances, the established type scale and each reader's local geometry when appearance changes.

rules.name: The Canvas Host Rule
rules.body: Within Canvas, host controls and task states use Synapse semantic surface, foreground, border and accent variables. The embedded editor owns shape menus, properties and page navigation; document colors remain document data.

rules.name: The Canvas Recovery Rule
rules.body: Within Canvas, file import requires an explicit replacement action and preserves one previous document with the block. Keep the recovery action available after saving and reopening, and keep unreadable source data intact.

dos: Do keep the AnuPpuccin preset separate from the incumbent Synapse palette and preserve explicit workspace selection.
Do preserve the imported AnuPpuccin color functions, readable accent ink and explicit folder/icon color precedence.
Do keep reading colors separate from font sizes, editor lifecycle and source Markdown.
Do use the semantic CSS variables and the existing icon family.
Do preserve the application shell while improving a local view.
Do theme focus, selection, scrolling and selected filters with established tokens.
Do keep the Tags extension scoped and use its readable context color for dense secondary labels.
Do preserve fixed row bounds, real tag-path hierarchy and explicit read-only preview actions in Tags.
Do keep selected-tag summaries bounded and expose the full removable selection through +N.
Do move focus into the visible pane after a narrow-layout pane switch.
Do keep All Notes type, context and corner roles scoped to the library.
Do use actual note excerpts when covers are absent, and keep editor and quick-reading actions explicit.
Do preserve measured-width windowing, visible focus and the return context in All Notes.
Do keep Files type, context, folder and corner roles scoped to the shared Files/Trash browser.
Do keep the current folder route and selection actions reachable in narrow Files layouts.
Do preserve fixed row bounds, folders-first ordering and mounted keyboard targets in Files and Trash.
Do load Files quick look only on request and describe Trash dates as modification dates.
Do keep workspace geometry and shape roles scoped to the shell while retaining each local view's container behavior.
Do use the existing link and secondary foreground roles for workspace text states.
Do keep shell controls reachable when panels collapse and preserve save-before-navigation behavior.
Do keep Calendar source, context, type and corner roles scoped to the calendar workspace.
Do preserve the displayed date anchor, bounded previews, complete paged day lists and focus restoration when changing visible Calendar regions.
Do pair Calendar source color with labels or icons and keep task editing, journal opening and external sending explicit.
donts: Don't turn a selectable AnuPpuccin preset into an implicit default migration.
Don't infer complete Obsidian plugin compatibility from the supported palette and reading/folder adaptation.
Don't let a local feature silently change the global palette or typography.
Don't impose decorative image covers or motion on dense note indexes.
Don't turn preview tag actions into note edits or load image covers while filtering Tags.
Don't invent file sizes or deletion timestamps in Files and Trash.
Don't treat Calendar's synthetic light-token capture as a shipped global application light theme.
